{{Short description|Invariant in mathematics}}
{{No footnotes|date=May 2017}}
In mathematical invariant theory, a '''transvectant''' is an [[Invariant (mathematics)|invariant]] formed from ''n'' invariants in ''n'' variables using [[Cayley's Ω process]].

==Definition==
If ''Q''<sub>1</sub>,...,''Q''<sub>''n''</sub> are functions of ''n'' variables '''x'''&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''x''<sub>1</sub>,...,''x''<sub>''n''</sub>) and ''r''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0  is an integer then the ''r''<sup>th</sup> transvectant of these functions is a function of ''n'' variables given by<math display="block"> \operatorname{Tr} \Omega^r(Q_1\otimes\cdots \otimes Q_n)</math>where<math display="block">
\Omega = \begin{vmatrix} \frac{\partial}{\partial x_{11}} & \cdots &\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{1n}} \\ \vdots& \ddots & \vdots\\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x_{n1}} & \cdots &\frac{\partial}{\partial x_{nn}}  \end{vmatrix}
</math>is [[Cayley's Ω process]], and the tensor product means take a product of functions with different variables '''x'''<sup>1</sup>,..., '''x'''<sup>''n''</sup>, and the [[trace operator]] Tr means setting all the vectors '''x'''<sup>''k''</sup> equal.

==Examples==
The zeroth transvectant is the product of the ''n'' functions.<math display="block"> \operatorname{Tr} \Omega^0(Q_1\otimes\cdots \otimes Q_n) = \prod_k Q_k</math>The first transvectant is the [[Jacobian determinant]] of the ''n'' functions.<math display="block"> \operatorname{Tr} \Omega^1(Q_1\otimes\cdots \otimes Q_n) = \det \begin{bmatrix} \partial_k Q_l \end{bmatrix}</math>The second transvectant is a constant times the completely polarized form of the [[Hessian matrix|Hessian]] of the ''n'' functions.

When <math>n = 2</math>, the binary transvectants have an explicit formula:{{sfn|Olver|1999|p=88}}<math display="block">\operatorname{Tr} \Omega^k( f \otimes g ) = \sum_{l=0}^k (-1)^l \binom kl \partial_x^{k-l} \partial_y^l f \partial_y^{k-l} \partial_l^l g</math>which can be more succinctly written as<math display="block">f \left(\overleftarrow{\partial_{x}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\partial_{y}}-\overleftarrow{\partial_{y}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\partial_{x}}\right)^k g</math>where the arrows denote the function to be taken the derivative of. This notation is used in [[Moyal product]].

== Applications ==
{{Math theorem
| math_statement = All polynomial covariants and invariants of any system of binary forms can be expressed as linear combinations of iterated transvectants.
| name = First Fundamental Theorem of Invariant Theory
| note = {{sfn|Olver|1999|p=90}}
}}
